examples.question_text:
Find the multiplication rule connecting the rows. Check every column.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Top}&2&5&8\\\hline\text{Bottom}&12&30&48\end{array}$
examples.solution_text:
Divide a bottom value by its matching top value:
$12\div2=6$.
Check the multiplier in every column:
$\begin{aligned}6\times2&=12\\6\times5&=30\\6\times8&=48\end{aligned}$
Bottom $=6\times$ top.

examples.question_text:
Find the multiplication rule and complete the table.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Top}&3&6&9\\\hline\text{Bottom}&21&42&\square\end{array}$
examples.solution_text:
$21\div3=7$.
Check the other complete column: $7\times6=42$.
Bottom $=7\times$ top.
For top $9$, the bottom value is $7\times9=63$.
The completed table is
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Top}&3&6&9\\\hline\text{Bottom}&21&42&63\end{array}$.

examples.question_text:
Find the multiplication rule and the missing top value.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Top}&2&\square&7\\\hline\text{Bottom}&16&40&56\end{array}$
examples.solution_text:
$16\div2=8$.
Check the other complete column: $8\times7=56$.
Bottom $=8\times$ top.
Reverse multiplication to find the missing top value:
$40\div8=5$.
Check: $8\times5=40$.
The completed table is
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Top}&2&5&7\\\hline\text{Bottom}&16&40&56\end{array}$.

examples.question_text:
Mia says the rule is bottom $=4\times$ top. Test her rule and give the correct multiplication rule.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Top}&3&4&7\\\hline\text{Bottom}&15&20&35\end{array}$
examples.solution_text:
Mia's rule fails in the first column: $4\times3=12$, but the bottom value is $15$.
Find the multiplier: $15\div3=5$.
Check every column:
$\begin{aligned}5\times3&=15\\5\times4&=20\\5\times7&=35\end{aligned}$
The correct rule is bottom $=5\times$ top.

examples.derivation: 12 ÷ 2 = 6; multiplying 2, 5 and 8 by 6 gives 12, 30 and 48. Bottom = 6 × top. This adapts the source's multiplicative table and every-column verification.
21 ÷ 3 = 7; 7 × 6 = 42 confirms the other complete column. The missing bottom value is 7 × 9 = 63. This matches Foundation Q3b's rule-and-completion task.
16 ÷ 2 = 8; 8 × 7 = 56 confirms the multiplier. The missing top value is 40 ÷ 8 = 5, checked by 8 × 5 = 40. This adapts Foundation Q4a's missing-input table.

The proposed multiplier fails because 4 × 3 = 12 rather than 15. Independently, 15 ÷ 3 = 5; 5 × 3 = 15, 5 × 4 = 20 and 5 × 7 = 35. Bottom = 5 × top. This applies the source's requirement that a rule satisfy every column.
